slice.leaf: Pin the smallest source-qualified Axum/Tower authentication seam that inserts a trusted server Principal into HTTP request extensions before rmcp-v3.1.4 StreamableHttpService splits the request into Parts, and give a fail-closed retrieval shape usable across RequestContext-bearing handlers.

observed_facts: The HTTP request is split with request.into_parts(); the resulting http::request::Parts is inserted into the MCP request extensions before OneshotTransport/handler dispatch on the evidenced Streamable HTTP paths.
The source documentation explicitly states that state added via axum's Extension layer is available inside Parts.extensions and shows RequestContext.extensions -> Parts -> Parts.extensions lookup.

sources.observed_fact: The official middleware example authenticates before next.run(req), inserts CurrentUser using req.extensions_mut().insert(current_user), and rejects unauthorized requests before the inner route executes.

slice.finding: The smallest qualified insertion seam is an outer Axum/Tower authentication middleware layer that wraps the route/service backed by rmcp StreamableHttpService and inserts a server-authenticated Principal into the HTTP Request.extensions before calling next.run(req). rmcp-v3.1.4 later preserves that extension by moving the entire http::request::Parts into MCP request extensions before dispatch. A handler can therefore recover the same Principal with a nested fail-closed lookup RequestContext.extensions.get::<http::request::Parts>() followed by parts.extensions.get::<Principal>(). This avoids trusting client _meta for identity and avoids duplicating identity propagation separately in call_tool/get_task/update_task/cancel_task handlers.

compile_risk_minimized_shape.auth_middleware: async fn auth(mut req: axum::extract::Request, next: axum::middleware::Next) -> Result<axum::response::Response, http::StatusCode> { let principal = authenticate(req.headers()).await.ok_or(http::StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED)?; req.extensions_mut().insert(principal); Ok(next.run(req).await) }
compile_risk_minimized_shape.layer_rule: Apply middleware::from_fn(auth) as a layer outside the MCP route/service so authentication and Principal insertion happen before StreamableHttpService::call receives the request.

fail_closed_conditions: No authenticated Principal inserted by trusted middleware -> handler rejects; never fall back to client metadata.
No http::request::Parts in RequestContext.extensions -> reject as unsupported/non-evidenced transport path.
Do not generalize this proof to non-Streamable-HTTP transports without a transport-specific server-authenticated identity seam.
scope_limits: This proves only identity propagation ordering for the exact rmcp-v3.1.4 StreamableHttpService paths evidenced by tower.rs plus canonical Axum middleware request-extension semantics.

It does not prove a concrete authentication backend, TLS/reverse-proxy trust boundary, router layer ordering for a specific rmcp example application, persistent task create-or-get, restart redrive, or effect-side idempotency/fencing.
The overall Phase-1 route still has an unresolved resident server/executor and persistent-task-runtime child; this slice is not Phase-1 acceptance.

acceptance_assessment.residual_richer_mode_protected_or_user_e: UNRESOLVED_OVERALL_ROUTE: application-owned resident HTTP/task executor and persistent task/redrive infrastructure remain unresolved; the Principal propagation seam itself adds no separate user execution handoff.
acceptance_assessment.quota_scope: The evidenced identity propagation mechanism is in-process Axum/http extension state and does not inherently consume hosted runner, Codespaces, artifact/LFS/package, cloud, API/model-credit, or other finite monthly quota. Full route acceptance remains blocked by executor/runtime obligations rather than quota evidence.
